text.content:
Warcraft is one of the most beloved and enduring fantasy franchises in the world. From the real-time strategy campaigns of the original Warcraft games to the sprawling world of World of Warcraft and beyond, Azeroth has been home to decades of epic stories, unforgettable characters, and some of the richest lore in all of fantasy gaming.

It is a world of continent-spanning wars, ancient gods sleeping beneath the earth, dragon aspects watching over mortal affairs, and heroes rising from every corner of a deeply detailed civilization.

Dragonbane is a fresh take to the classic Swedish tabletop roleplaying game Drakar och Demoner. It's a game about telling collaborative stories, making interesting choices, and bringing characters to life in ways no video game ever could.

Bane of Azeroth is a collection of homebrew content that brings the Warcraft setting to Dragonbane, allowing you and your friends to become true heroes of Azeroth, not guided through a predetermined questline, but free to forge your own legend in a world you already know and love.

Why Azeroth?

Azeroth is a remarkable setting for a tabletop campaign. It has everything a great Dragonbane world needs: a rich history stretching back tens of thousands of years, a geography packed with distinct and memorable regions, factions in constant tension with each other, and an enormous cast of cultures, kin, and characters whose stories are still unfolding.

Whether your party wants to investigate a conspiracy in Stormwind, explore the ancient ruins of a fallen troll empire, broker a fragile peace between the Horde and the Alliance, or delve into the depths of a titan facility that no one has entered in millennia, Azeroth can support it.

And unlike in World of Warcraft itself, you aren't on rails. You don't have to follow the questline. When your party walks into Blackrock Mountain, you don't have to fight your way through a dungeon in a fixed order. You can talk to the Dark Iron dwarves, learn about their history, figure out what Ragnaros actually wants, and decide for yourselves how to handle it. The story of your campaign is yours to write.

Dragonbane gives you the tools to do that, and Azeroth gives you an incredibly rich world to do it in.

What is this book?

Bane of Azeroth is a player options supplement for Dragonbane. It presents everything you need to create a hero of Azeroth: new kin drawn from Warcraft's many peoples, heroic abilities that capture Warcraft's iconic class identities, and new spells and minions to support those abilities.

This book is designed to be fully compatible with existing Dragonbane content. It does not replace the core rules of Dragonbane. You will still use Dragonbane professions, spells, equipment, rules, and everything else. Bane of Azeroth is purely additive. You can use as much or as little of it as you like, mix it freely with content from any other Dragonbane supplement, and combine it with the full range of existing Dragonbane options. A character built entirely from Bane of Azeroth content will work seamlessly alongside one built from the core rules alone.

Bane of Azeroth contains the following new player options:

  • Kin. New Warcraft-inspired kin covering the major peoples of Azeroth, each with one or more innate abilities.
  • Heroic Class Abilities. One free heroic ability for each of the standard World of Warcraft classes, designed to add Warcraft identity and gameplay to the already existing professions. In addition, there are three more heroic abilities per World of Warcraft class that can be selected whenever you gain heroic abilities during your adventures, to further strengthen the Warcraft identity.
  • Gear. A small selection of Warcraft-inspired weapons and gear.
  • Spells. New spells to complement certain heroic class abilities, available to players with the appropriate heroic abilities.
  • Companions. New common animals available to those with the COMPANION heroic ability and demons that a Warlock can summon.

Design Goals

Bane of Azeroth is not a faithful one-to-one translation of World of Warcraft into Dragonbane. That is intentional. World of Warcraft is an MMORPG designed around different priorities: it needs to balance tens of thousands of simultaneous players, deliver reliable repeatable content, and express class fantasy through a very specific set of rotations and mechanics. Dragonbane is a collaborative storytelling game built around narrative flexibility, character expression, and player agency. The two games are excellent at very different things.

The goal of Bane of Azeroth is not to make Dragonbane feel like World of Warcraft; the goal is to make the best version of Dragonbane that happens to take place in the Warcraft setting. That means drawing on Warcraft's lore, aesthetics, and class identities for inspiration, while building mechanics that feel natural and fun in a Dragonbane context rather than trying to force a video game into a tabletop mold.

With that in mind, the design principles for Bane of Azeroth are:

  • Start with Dragonbane. All Bane of Azeroth content begins with standard Dragonbane core rules, and design patterns. Warcraft flavor is layered on top and does not replace the foundation.
  • Keep it simple. Warcraft contains an enormous mount of content, and trying to faithfully implement every talent tree and ability interaction would make for a sprawling, unplayable mess. Bane of Azeroth picks core fantasies and builds around them, even if that means leaving a lot of inspiration on the table.
  • Use Dragonbane's vocabulary. The game already has well-established ways of expressing certain ideas. Bane of Azeroth uses those conventions rather than fighting them, so that new content feels like a natural part of the game rather than a foreign object.
  • Balance matters, but fun matters more. The goal is to make sure Bane of Azeroth content is competitive with standard Dragonbane content, internally consistent, on par with characters created through the core rules of Dragonbane. But balance in service of a dull experience is worth nothing. If something needs a little extra oomph to deliver the right Warcraft feeling, it gets it.

Buy-In and Creativity

Playing Bane of Azeroth rewards a certain amount of creative buy-in from both players and DMs. The rules give you a framework, but the full experience comes from leaning into the fiction. Spell casting in Dragonbane is primarily part of one professions that in Bane of Azeroth is the prerequisite for several heroic class abilities. A player opting for the shadow priest fantasy might learn different spells than a player going for the holy priest fantasy.

If you have access to the Book of Magic supplement, the increased variety in that book is great for helping spell caster classes getting more distinguished than using just the core rules, but this supplement works either way.

On the Dungeon Master's side, a little flexibility goes a long way: if a player has a clear and reasonable vision for their character, accommodating small requests that help bring that vision to life is usually worth it. If a paladin player wants to pick up a school of magic for increasing their healing capacity (by picking the MAGIC TALENT heroic ability), maybe the skill is granted by the Light and does not require the character to seek out training.

The goal is a game that feels like Warcraft in the ways that matter most to your table.

Contact and More

I welcome any and all feedback, comments, questions, etc. on any of my work! You can reach me on Discord, primarily via either the Champions of Azeroth server or the Dragonbane Community server. In both places I go by Auvreannia. There is currently no dedicated Discord server for Bane of Azeroth, but there might be one in the future if this becomes popular enough.

Thanks for reading, and may all your adventures be legendary!

There are 14 playable kin in Azeroth. Humans and Orcs are the most common kin, but you are free to choose any of them. You can also roll your kin using one of the tables below. All kin are briefly described below.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoATblKinAnyFac1]{Any Faction}

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoATblKinAllianc]{Alliance}

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoATblKinHorde01]{Horde}

Language

All player characters in Azeroth can speak, read, and write a common language, which for simplicity's sake is called the common tongue for alliance, and orcish for the horde. Most creatures the player characters encounter know these languages, but there may be exceptions. Non-human kin often have their own languages that few humans understand. To understand other languages, the LANGUAGES skill is used. At the GMs discretion, the common tongue might be used for all player characters if they don't want to segregate by faction.

Dracthyr

The dracthyr are an ancient race of humanoid dragonkin created by the black Dragon Aspect Neltharion, who combined the essence of dragons with the adaptability of mortal races to forge ideal soldiers. Long ago, the dracthyr were put into a long slumber, only to awaken millennia later as new threats emerged. Organized into tightly bonded weyrns, the dracthyr now seek to reclaim what they have lost and forge their own path in a changing Azeroth. Each dracthyr has a visage, a unique humanoid appearance they can turn into.

Ability: Draconic Wings

Willpower Points: Varies

By spending 3 willpower, you can move freely through the air during your turn. If you end your turn mid air, you safely land in the closest free space below you.

When @UUID[JournalEntry.SbbSMsuvWeo3HaID.JournalEntryPage.6WPxPxUjh4W80RNy#falling]{falling}, you can spend 1 willpower to slow your fall and land as light as a feather, no matter the height.

Ability: Visage

Willpower Points: -

By activating this ability (a free action in combat) you change between your dracthyr form and visage. It has no effect on your game statistics.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameDracthyr1]{Name - Dracthyr}

Draenei

Driven from their home world of Argus, the honorable draenei fled the wrath of the Burning Legion for eons before eventually finding a new home on Azeroth. Draenei are tall, bipedal ungulates with blue skin, hooves, tails, and horns and tendrils adorning their faces. Their glowing eyes reveal their deep connection to the Light, which enables them to wield powerful magic for healing and protection. Despite enduring persecution and hardship across multiple worlds, they remain resilient and noble, embodying traits of kindness, compassion, and justice. Their alien perspective, shaped by their nomadic, nigh-immortal existence, grants them unique insights and makes them valuable allies in the ongoing struggle against evil.

Ability: Heroic Presence

Willpower Points: 3

Activating this ability (an action in combat) gives all allies within 10 meters a boon to all rolls and heals the Scared condition. The boon lasts until your turn in the next round.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameDraenei01]{Name - Draenei}

Dwarf

Bold and adventurous, dwarves are a hardy people who relish battle, craftsmanship, and exploration. Dwarves are stocky and powerfully built despite their short stature, and often sport intricate, well-groomed beards. They have a rich cultural heritage steeped in tradition and craftsmanship, with a particular fondness for mining, smithing, and engineering. Dwarves value loyalty, courage, and honor above all else, and they are fiercely protective of their clans and homelands. Despite their gruff exterior, dwarves possess a deep sense of camaraderie and kinship, making them stalwart allies and formidable adversaries alike.

Bronzebeard

The Bronzebeard clan is preeminent among the various Ironforge dwarf clans of Khaz Modan. During the War of the Three Hammers, they led the dwarves of Ironforge against Thaurissan and the Dark Iron clan. Bronzebeard dwarves are accustomed to the icy climes of Khaz Modan, and are especially attuned to their Titan-forged history.

Ability: Stoneform

Willpower Points: 3

Your skin turns hard and gray, and any non-magical damage is halved (rounded up). The effect lasts until your turn in the next round. You can activate this ability as a reaction when you are hit by an attack.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameBronzebrd]{Name - Bronzebeard}

Dark Iron

Known for their fiery tempers and fierce determination, Dark Iron dwarves have a turbulent history with the other clans. They have gray or black skin, and their hair can glow red. A failed coup in Ironforge ignited the War of the Three Hammers, and many of the Dark Iron once fought in the service of Ragnaros the Firelord. Now the Dark Iron clan is united behind Queen-Regent Moira Thaurissan, and have pledged their martial and magical might to the Alliance.

Ability: Fireblood

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability (no action) when making an attack roll and get a boon to the roll. You also heal a condition of your choice.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameDarkIron1]{Name - Dark Iron}

Elf

The elves of Azeroth trace their origins to the mystical Well of Eternity, a source of unimaginable arcane power that shaped their society and granted them unparalleled mastery of magic. Over time, their civilization flourished, becoming the dominant force on Azeroth. However, their society shattered during the Sundering, eventually leading to numerous diverse factions and heritages. Elves are typically tall and slender with long pointed ears, and are known for their incredible longevity, keen senses, and exceptional mastery of both war and magic. Elves now find themselves torn between their glorious past and an uncertain future.

Blood Elf

For millennia, high elves thrived in the magical kingdom of Quel'thalas until the arrival of the Scourge decimated their civilization. The destruction of the Sunwell, their source of power, led to their near-extinction. Renamed blood elves or sin'dorei, they seek to reclaim their lost powers and heritage. Blood elves typically possess fair skin and brilliant gold or crimson hair, distinguishing them from their elven kin.

Ability: Arcane Affinity

Willpower Points: 2

You cast one of the @UUID[JournalEntry.BHzSGEPaCGVadFsb.JournalEntryPage.cvFSLoFtdJOQcxtU#magic-tricks]{Magic Tricks} listed under General Magic. To determine success, roll against any school of magic, or LANGUAGES, whichever is higher.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameBloodElf1]{Name - Blood Elf}

Night Elf

Ten thousand years ago, the kaldorei, or night elves, founded a vast empire, but their reckless use of primal magic brought them to ruin. They retreated to the forests, isolated until the return of the Burning Legion forced them into action. Night elves are easily recognized by their purple or blue skin, and hair that can range from natural greens to twilight purples. With bow, blade, or claw, night elves are fierce defenders of the natural world, and unforgiving enemies of those that would abuse it.

Ability: Shadowmeld

Willpower Points: 2

Instead of making a SNEAKING roll you can activate this ability to automatically succeed as if you had rolled a dragon.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameNightElf1]{Name - Night Elf}

Gnome

Gnomes are a small, highly intelligent species renowned for their technological expertise. Originating from Gnomeregan, they have a rich history of innovation and engineering, contributing significantly to the Alliance's technological advancements. Physically, gnomes are diminutive with large heads, short limbs, and often wild and colorful hair. Despite their small stature, gnomes are formidable inventors and loyal allies, and have

distinguished themselves time and time again with their ingenuity, bravery, and loyalty.

Ability: Escape Artist

Willpower Points: 2

You get a boon on opposing a grapple attempt. Or you get a boon on breaking free from a grapple, which can be attempted as a free action.

If the optional rules for grapple is not used, the gnome can get the @UUID[Item.GiE0TwixaYnxFT6i]{Hard to Catch} ability from the core rules HALFLING instead.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameGnome0001]{Name - Gnome}

Goblin

Goblins are a cunning and entrepreneurial species, originating from the Isle of Kezan where they overthrew their troll overlords using their guile and genius. Physically, they are small, green-skinned creatures with sharp teeth and a hunched posture. Known for their resourcefulness and greed, goblins excel in trade, technology, and explosive inventions. Despite their mercenary nature, they have become valuable, if expensive allies to both the Horde and the Alliance during Azeroth's many conflicts.

Ability: Rocket Jump

Willpower Points: 1

You can leap five times as far as your normal leaping distance, horizontally or vertically. This might render an ACROBATICS roll for climbing unecessary if the obstactle is lower than the distance you leap.

Alternatively, you can dash as a free action.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameGoblin001]{Name - Goblin}

Human

The young humans have a rich history marked by resilience and adaptability. Emerging from scattered tribes, they founded mighty kingdoms like Stormwind and Kul Tiras. Their appearance varies widely, with diverse skin tones, hair colors, and heights. Humans are driven by community, ambition, and values of courage and honor. Despite internal conflicts, they often unite against common threats, displaying acts of bravery and heroism in the face of adversity. Their ability to adapt and thrive in changing circumstances has made them a vital force in shaping the destiny of Azeroth.

Ability: Resourceful

Willpower Points: 3

When rolling for a skill, you can choose to make the roll using another skill of your choice. You must be able to justify how you use the selected skill instead of the normal one. The GM has the final word, but should be lenient.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameHuman0001]{Name - Human}

Orc

While the proud, fearsome orcs have spread across Azeroth, they originated on the planet Draenor. A peaceful people with shamanic beliefs, they were enslaved by the Burning Legion and forced into war with the humans of Azeroth. Although it took many years, the orcs finally escaped the demons' corruption and won their freedom. To this day they fight for honor in a world that hates and reviles them, having forged a new home and family in the mighty Horde. With their muscular builds, prominent tusks, and varied skin tones ranging from green to brown, orcs remain fierce and eager for battle, valuing strength and honor above all.

Ability: Relentless

Willpower Points: 3

If you have zero HP, you can activate this ability to automatically @UUID[JournalEntry.SbbSMsuvWeo3HaID.JournalEntryPage.CJjqkHzpow39ViUi#death]{rally} (no action), without rolling against WIL or being persuaded by someone else.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameOrc000001]{Name - Orc}

Pandaren

Veiled in myth and legend, the enigmatic pandaren remain a mystery to most of Azeroth. Their noble history spans thousands of years, predating human empires and even the Sundering. Native to Pandaria, their homeland vanished behind a shrouding mist during that cataclysm. A second pandaren civilization thrives aboard the giant turtle Shen-zin Su, known as the “Wandering Isle.” Unlike their secluded kin, these pandaren roam Azeroth's seas in search of adventure.

Ability: Inner Peace

Willpower Points: -

You can meditate deeply during a stretch rest. You heal an additional D6 HP and a D6 extra WP, and can recover from an additional condition. You are completely unresponsive during your meditation and cannot be awakened.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANamePandaren1]{Name - Pandaren}

Tauren

With a proud nomadic tradition, the mighty tauren have roamed across Azeroth. From the vast plains of Mulgore to the rugged peaks of Highmountain and beyond, they embody a reverence for nature and ancestral wisdom. Towering in stature with bovine features and tribal adornments, they evoke a primal aura. Tauren prioritize harmony and balance, serving as fierce defenders of nature and their kin. Despite their imposing presence, they possess a gentle spirit and deep connection to the Earth Mother. Their culture emphasizes wisdom, spirituality, and community, shaping them into compassionate allies and formidable foes alike.

Ability: War Stomp

Willpower Points: 3

You can, as an action in combat, slam your hooves into the ground. Make a BRAWLING attack with a bane against all creatures within 2 meters, rolling only once to hit. Each creature hit takes D6 damage and falls to the ground. Roll damage separately for each creature.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameTauren001]{Name - Tauren}

Troll

Shrouded in ancient lore and mystique, trolls have a history as diverse as their many tribes scattered across Azeroth. With lithe frames, vividly colored skin, and elongated tusks, they exude a wild and primal aura. Trolls revere ancient gods and ancestral spirits, their culture steeped in tradition and spirituality. Fierce warriors and cunning hunters, they thrive in both shadow and sunlight, adapting to various environments with ease. Despite their tribal conflicts, trolls value unity and kinship within their clans. With a resilience honed through generations of survival, they remain formidable adversaries and steadfast allies in the ever-changing world of Azeroth.

Ability: Regeneration

Willpower Points: 3

By activating this ability (a free action in combat) you heal D6 HP. This can be combined with @UUID[Item.SY62xmX9uBVml786]{Fast Healer} for 2D6 HP healed.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameTroll0001]{Name - Troll}

Undead

When the Scourge marched across Azeroth, it added to its ranks by raising many of its victims to undeath. Many are mindless husks of their former selves, some possess intelligence but are bound to the Scourge, while others have managed to free themselves from the Lich King's will. The Undead kin can be used for any intelligent creature that has been raised to undeath, whether they were animated by the Scourge or by other necromantic means.

Ability: Touch of the Grave

Willpower Points: 3

Instead of making a @UUID[JournalEntry.SbbSMsuvWeo3HaID.JournalEntryPage.CJjqkHzpow39ViUi#death]{Death Roll} you can activate this ability to automatically succeed as if you had rolled a dragon.

Ability: Undead Nature

Willpower Points: -

You don't need to eat, drink or breathe.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameUndead001]{Name - Undead}

Vulpera

Native to the desolate sands of Vol'dun, vulpera are known for their resourcefulness, creativity, and cunning. With fox-like features and small but agile builds, they navigate the harsh desert terrain with ease. Skilled traders and negotiators, vulpera excel in finding solutions to problems and exploiting opportunities for profit. Their history is marked by a legacy of survival and adaptation, as they thrive amidst danger and uncertainty. Despite their diminutive size, vulpera possess a fierce determination to overcome challenges and safeguard their way of life.

Ability: Luck

Willpower Points: 3

You re-roll one D20 roll, that did not result in a demon, and must use the new result. If you have boons or banes, you must re-roll all dice. This can be used in combination with @UUID[JournalEntry.V4R4dCuKSK2mi8RF.JournalEntryPage.eIQgHhYPUczg7kbZ#pushing-your-roll]{Pushing your Roll}, potentially re-rolling the same roll twice.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameVulpera01]{Name - Vulpera}

Worgen

Worgen are large, lupine humanoids that walk upright, hunt and howl like wolves, and can run on all fours. Their origins lie in an ancient curse born from an night elf druidic ritual seeking to harness the fury of the wolf. Thought lost, the curse resurfaced in Gilneas, transforming those bitten or who drink worgen blood. Without control, the afflicted may succumb to mindless ferocity, but with discipline, medication, and magic, some retain a semblance of their former selves.

Ability: Darkflight

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability (no action) when making an attack roll and get a boon to the roll. You also become Angry, if you're not already. You can take the dash action as part of the attack action, moving before or after the attack.

Ability: Two Forms

Willpower Points: 1

By activating this ability (a free action in combat) you change between your humanoid and worgen forms. When in humanoid form, your movement and kin abilities other than this one is the same as if your kin was @UUID[JournalEntry.BoAJrnlPlayerOpt.JournalEntryPage.BoAPgPlayerKin01#human]{Human}.

@DisplayTable[RollTable.BoANameWorgen001]{Name - Worgen}

Traditionally, games set in Azeroth use classes. Classes are not a concept in Dragonbane. To represent the traditional classes of Azeroth, this supplement provides a set of heroic abilities. In addition to choosing a profession when creating your player character, choose one heroic class ability from this chapter that you start the game with. You must fulfill the requirement for the heroic ability you choose. You are now part of the class from which you chose a heroic ability.

When you gain heroic abilities during play, you can also choose heroic abilities from your class. You can only ever be part of one class unless your GM says otherwise. World of Warcraft limits which kin can choose certain classes. Bane of Azeroth does not impose such limitations by default, but the GM may do so, for example by limiting Demon Hunters to Elf kin.

The heroic ability gained through this chapter makes a character somewhat more powerful than a character created using only the Dragonbane core rules. It is equivalent to granting one extra heroic ability at character creation. If a campaign combines characters created with and without Bane of Azeroth, grant the other characters one extra starting heroic ability to keep them equivalent.

Death Knight

Death knights are among the most feared warriors in Azeroth's history. Created by the Lich King to serve as his most elite soldiers, death knights wield unholy magic, runic power, and the mastery of undeath that their master bestowed upon them. They are not undead in the traditional sense. They are fallen champions, raised and remade, their mortal lives extinguished and replaced with something colder and more terrible.

Over time, many death knights have broken free of the Lich King's domination, and these liberated champions now fight for their own purposes, carrying the weight of what they once were.

@UUID[Item.p2qUveF2aGom0pOU]{Death Knight's Rebirth}

Requirement: Axes, Hammers, or Swords 12

Willpower Points: —

You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. You know how to engrave necromantic runes into a melee weapon. Engraving a rune takes a stretch and replaces any runes you have already engraved, in the same weapon or a different one. You gain the benefits of your chosen rune listed below.

  • Fallen Crusader: Whenever you deal damage to a living creature with the weapon, you heal 1 HP.
  • Razorice: The weapon is cold to the touch, and attacks with it count as magical.
  • Unending Thirst: While wielding the weapon, your movement rate increases by 2.

@UUID[Item.ttKCQkUBUcINj3Od]{Death Grip}

Requirement: Death Knight's Rebirth

Willpower Points: 2

You harness the energy that surrounds and binds all matter. If an enemy and another player character are both within 10 meters of you and the enemy tries to attack the other character, you can activate this ability to pull the enemy toward you and make it attack you instead. Using this ability can be done out of turn and does not count as an action.

@UUID[Item.B9grTl5KOi08GNba]{Frostreaper}

Requirement: Death Knight's Rebirth

Willpower Points: 2

By activating this ability, you emanate a frosty aura, chilling the air around you. Until your turn in the next round, any living creature that moves within 10 meters of you has its movement rate halved, and if it ends its turn within the aura, it must roll BUSHCRAFT to resist cold.

@UUID[Item.Dn7a4K6UfKAfgek8]{Raise Ghoul}

Requirement: Death Knight's Rebirth

Willpower Points: 3

This ability requires a stretch of time to raise a fallen creature into a ravenous @UUID[Actor.GhoulAct6Kp9T2xP]{ghoul}. The ghoul takes the form of an undead humanoid and counts as a monster in combat. It follows your commands (free action) and acts independently with its own initiative. The ghoul cannot heal HP, and it crumbles to dust and dies if it is ever out of your sight for a stretch of time, or if you use this ability again.

Demon Hunter

The demon hunters of the Illidari are among the most extreme and controversial figures in Azeroth. Trained by Illidan Stormrage himself, they sacrificed their eyes and much of their identity to consume the essence of demons, turning the Burning Legion's power against itself. They are elves, night elves and blood elves, who chose a path that most of their kin consider monstrous, and who carry that stigma alongside their extraordinary power.

Marked by their blindfolds, their tattoos, and the fel energy that burns within them, demon hunters are warriors walking a permanent razor's edge between themselves and the void they consumed.

@UUID[Item.eG3wRvDISSUGLfnc]{Demon Hunter Initiation}

Requirement: Axes, Brawling, Knives, or Swords 12

Willpower Points: —

Your infernal metamorphosis gives you advantages in your hunt for demons. Your demonic wings make you glide horizontally instead of falling. Subtract your movement rate from the falling distance before determining falling damage. Your glowing eyes let you ignore the effects of darkness, and you always know whether a creature you are looking at is a demon.

@UUID[Item.2aVCfwfEPjZojAgI]{Eye Beam}

Requirement: Demon Hunter Initiation

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability to make your eyes shoot laser beams at a creature within 20 meters. The attack automatically hits and cannot be parried. It deals 2D8 damage and is considered magical.

@UUID[Item.LbTGlaive7wQ3xN2]{Live by the Glaive}

Requirement: Demon Hunter Initiation

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability (no action) when you make a successful parry to turn the roll into a dragon.

@UUID[Item.SoulCleave4mR8kZ]{Soul Cleave}

Requirement: Demon Hunter Initiation

Willpower Points: 2

If you deal damage with an attack to a living creature, you can activate this ability (no action) to heal yourself for the same amount of HP as the target takes in damage.

Druid

The druids of Azeroth are among its oldest and most mysterious guardians. Trained in the traditions passed down from Malfurion Stormrage and the Cenarion Circle, they draw power from the natural world and from the Emerald Dream, the spiritual reflection of Azeroth as it was meant to be. Druids are shapeshifters, healers, and spellcasters, equally at home in bear form defending their allies, in cat form stalking prey through the undergrowth, or calling down starfire from the sky in the form of the moonkin.

Their connection to nature runs deep, and their patience runs deeper still.

@UUID[Item.7XGIwTKnDqE3ZvhD]{Druidic Awakening}

Requirement: One School of Magic

Willpower Points: —

You know the general spell @UUID[Item.SavIncarn6e7f8g9]{Savage Incarnation}. This spell is always prepared and does not count toward the number of spells you can hold prepared in your memory.

When you sleep, you enter a dream state that allows you to stay alert to your surroundings during a shift rest, and you can awaken instantly and at will.

@UUID[Item.jSyoPlsXX9CcOBQi]{Chosen of Elune}

Requirement: Druidic Awakening

Willpower Points: —

You know the general spell @UUID[Item.StarsInc6AbCdE7f]{Incarnation of the Stars}. This spell is always prepared and does not count toward the number of spells you can hold prepared in your memory.

@UUID[Item.cy4TSMJQKlR1RG5w]{King of the Jungle}

Requirement: Druidic Awakening

Willpower Points: —

You know the general spell @UUID[Item.FeralInc2OpQrS3t]{Feral Incarnation}. This spell is always prepared and does not count toward the number of spells you can hold prepared in your memory.

@UUID[Item.1zM1M11RvPrqc6F7]{Tree of Life}

Requirement: Druidic Awakening

Willpower Points: —

You know the general spell @UUID[Item.Harmony4UvWxY5zQ]{Incarnation of Harmony}. This spell is always prepared and does not count toward the number of spells you can hold prepared in your memory.

Evoker

The dracthyr evokers are something unique in Azeroth: beings created specifically to wield the combined magical legacy of all five dragonflights. Born from Neltharion's ambition, they were designed as weapons and then sealed away, only to awaken in a changed world. As evokers, they have learned to channel draconic magic through their breath, fire and frost and arcane and time and life, in ways no other spellcaster can match.

They are simultaneously ancient and new, carrying the power of dragonkind in mortal form.

@UUID[Item.bdF6vg1SjBITnwG5]{Evoker's Legacy}

Requirement: One School of Magic

Willpower Points: —

Whenever you cast a spell at a power level higher than 1, the cost per power level is reduced to one for every level above the first (2 WP for power level 1, 3 WP for power level 2, and 4 WP for power level 3).

@UUID[Item.Sl2btNo06MMQTCQj]{Ebon Might}

Requirement: Evoker's Legacy

Willpower Points: 2

You can activate this ability when you cast a spell to give all allies within 10 meters a boon to all rolls. The boon lasts until your turn in the next round.

@UUID[Item.ao1H1pN9eKBVLBON]{Rewind}

Requirement: Evoker's Legacy

Willpower Points: 3

You can use your action to restore your own health or an ally's health to the value it had at the start of the last round.

@UUID[Item.KbZ487TZTcV7Em9H]{Tailwind}

Requirement: Evoker's Legacy

Willpower Points: 1

You can activate this ability on your turn to make the @UUID[JournalEntry.SbbSMsuvWeo3HaID.JournalEntryPage.KrSXg7HKmfo7xRcI#movement]{dash} action a free action during that turn.

Hunter

Hunters are Azeroth's masters of the wild. They are trackers and survivalists, archers and beast tamers, operating at the boundary between civilization and the untamed places of the world. What sets a hunter apart is the bond they form with their animal companions, a relationship built on trust, training, and something deeper that defies easy explanation.

Whether they prefer to fight alongside their beasts, pick off enemies from a distance, or lay traps and engage in close-quarters combat, hunters are among the most self-sufficient fighters in all of Azeroth.

@UUID[Item.blFEw7MLkYlNpsy4]{Hunter's Instincts}

Requirement: Companion Heroic Ability

Willpower Points: —

Your companion follows you even if you leave its natural environment. While it is within 50 meters of you, you can communicate with it telepathically. As an action, you can spend 1 WP to see through the companion's eyes and hear what it hears for one minute, gaining the benefits of any special senses it has. The WP cost for commanding the companion to attack is reduced to 2.

@UUID[Item.wZM2eY9eN6xdqL5d]{Aimed Shot}

Requirement: Hunter's Instincts

Willpower Points: 3

A strike with a two-handed ranged weapon inflicts D8 additional points of damage, but you cannot move in the same round. You can activate this ability after the roll to hit, but not if you moved. This can be combined with @UUID[Item.J6l8QwCJhBirvg03]{Twin Shot}.

@UUID[Item.ANfryDC2vUzxKJz5]{Beast Master}

Requirement: Hunter's Instincts

Willpower Points: 2

You can activate this ability when you or your companion is hit to transfer half the damage received (rounded down) to the other party, sharing the pain. You can do so after the roll for damage.

Alternatively, you can use an action to activate this ability to revive a fallen companion, as long as it happens within a shift of its death. If its body is within sight, it appears at the body; otherwise, it appears within 2 meters of you. It recovers1 [[/roll D6]] HP.

@UUID[Item.MbV2u8CdnDwZkyS6]{Superior Trapper}

Requirement: Hunter's Instincts

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability (no action) when a non-monster creature voluntarily moves to within 2 meters of you. The creature has to make an EVADE roll, and if it fails it either takes [[/roll 2d8]] damage as it burns or loses its actions and movement for the rest of the round as it is frozen in place (your choice).

Mage

The mages of Azeroth are among the most powerful and most dangerous individuals in the world. Trained in the traditions of Dalaran and the arcane schools that predate it, they manipulate the raw fabric of reality through the force of intellect and will.

Azeroth's mages come in many forms: frost mages who encrust their enemies in ice and slow time itself, fire mages who hurl blazing pyroblasts and ignite the air around their targets, and arcane mages who ride waves of pure magical force in surging blasts of focused power. What they share is a commitment to the study of magic as a discipline, and an awareness, sometimes ignored, of the danger that comes with wielding it.

@UUID[Item.f9Mta7M9w8ruZSL0]{Mage's Brilliance}

Requirement: One School of Magic

Willpower Points: —

You know the @UUID[Item.RPnxXYVb8z7EG5Wl]{Sense Magic} magic trick and can cast it without spending Willpower Points. Whenever you roll for LANGUAGES, you can choose the result 10 instead of rolling.

@UUID[Item.2JTCWcZSE25ZK2wg]{Ice Block}

Requirement: Mage's Brilliance

Willpower Points: 2

You can activate this ability when you are about to take damage (no action). You become immune to damage this round and the next, including the damage that triggered this ability. For this duration, you are frozen in place and cannot move or take any actions. You can activate this ability after it has been determined that you are hit, but before the roll for damage.

@UUID[Item.chlnu7rRBXdsaqRP]{Living Bomb}

Requirement: Mage's Brilliance

Willpower Points: 3

When you deal damage with a spell or this ability, you can choose an additional creature within 10 meters of the target that did not take damage from that spell or this ability. That creature takes the same damage (roll separately). You can use this multiple times for the same spell casting, as long as you can pay the Willpower Points for each use.

@UUID[Item.MaZ4ltolYbPEVuJd]{Time Warp}

Requirement: Mage's Brilliance

Willpower Points: 2

You can activate this ability at the start of another player character's or NPC's turn. You swap initiative cards with that player character or NPC (or group of NPCs acting on the same turn), and it cannot refuse. A monster with multiple turns swaps only the card of the current turn with yours. You act immediately.

Monk

The monks of Azeroth walk the path of the Pandaren, a martial tradition that arrived with the opening of Pandaria and spread quickly to students across both the Horde and the Alliance. Monks blend physical discipline with the manipulation of chi, a spiritual life force that flows through all living things, to achieve extraordinary feats of combat, healing, and focus.

Brewmasters fight with an improbable combination of acrobatics and alcoholic combustion; mistweavers channel chi into restorative mists that mend wounds at a distance; windwalkers strike with devastating speed, turning the flow of a fight with a single perfectly placed blow.

@UUID[Item.5lf9dHIKVBA2AoGM]{Monk's Serenity}

Requirement: Brawling 12

Willpower Points: —

The damage of your unarmed attacks increases to D10. If you use @UUID[Item.O7p7ZWnZNgxP8PFw]{Iron Fist}, the damage increases to 2D10 for that unarmed attack. You can also parry both melee and ranged attacks unarmed. When parrying, you roll against your skill level for BRAWLING.

@UUID[Item.Rt1ZUmUjltFEktWm]{Combo Strikes}

Requirement: Monk's Serenity

Willpower Points: 3

You activate this ability on your turn in combat when performing an unarmed attack, and you can then perform two extra unarmed attacks. The second and third attacks are made with a bane. Finish the first attack, including damage, before rolling the second one, and finish the second attack, including damage, before rolling the third one.

@UUID[Item.gzlUuHeXUc6Hd7zV]{Soothing Mist}

Requirement: Monk's Serenity

Willpower Points: 2

When you deal damage with an unarmed attack, you can activate this ability to heal another creature within 10 meters of you by the same amount.

@UUID[Item.9P7deH0tDnisRMem]{Stagger}

Requirement: Monk's Serenity

Willpower Points: 1

When you take damage in combat, you can activate this ability (no action). The damage is halved (rounded up). The next time you take damage in this round, you also take the damage that was reduced by this ability.

Paladin

The paladins of Azeroth are the champions of the Holy Light, warriors who have dedicated themselves to the service of faith and justice, and who wield divine power alongside their martial skill. The Light responds to belief rather than to any specific deity, making Azeroth's paladin tradition broader and more varied than it might appear.

A dwarf Vindicator of the Alliance, a Sunwalker tauren who worships An'she the sun spirit, and a blood elf Blood Knight who once stole their power from a captive Naaru are all paladins, despite their very different relationships to faith. What they share is conviction, and the power that conviction generates.

@UUID[Item.uWDdnL6xNT6peQdh]{Paladin's Righteousness}

Requirement: Hammers, Spears, or Swords 12

Willpower Points: —

Whenever you spend WP, you heal yourself or an ally within 2 meters by the same amount. You also always know whether a creature you are looking at is undead.

@UUID[Item.SwcTAB0V7Kui8IDr]{Avenger's Shield}

Requirement: Paladin's Righteousness

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability as an action if you are wielding a shield. You hurl your shield at a creature within 10 meters, and it then bounces to a creature of your choice within 10 meters of the first target, and again to a third creature within 10 meters of the second target. It then returns to your hand. Make separate attacks with your shield against all three targets with a bane. Finish the first attack, including damage, before rolling the second one, and finish the second one, including damage, before rolling the third one. Creatures that are hit have a bane when attacking any creature other than you until your turn in the next round.

@UUID[Item.AndvvqU6bjH1YwZk]{Beacon of Light}

Requirement: Paladin's Righteousness

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability as an action, making an allied creature within 10 meters a beacon of light. For a stretch of time, whenever you heal yourself or an ally, the beacon of light heals the same amount of HP. This ability also benefits from the HP restored by Paladin's Righteousness when activating this ability.

@UUID[Item.2MvSQhUyotNYLFwy]{Blade of Justice}

Requirement: Paladin's Righteousness

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability when you hit an enemy with a melee weapon, but before rolling for damage. The attack deals an extra D8 damage, or 2D8 damage to an undead target, and is considered magical.

Priest

The priests of Azeroth are channelers of divine power in all its forms, from the brilliant radiance of the Holy Light to the consuming shadows of the Void. Holy priests are beacons of hope on the battlefield, mending wounds and bolstering spirits with restorative magic. Discipline priests weave protective wards and sacred power words into their spellcasting, shielding allies as they fight.

Shadow priests abandon the light entirely, plumbing the depths of the Void for destructive psychic power that corrodes the minds and bodies of their enemies. All three traditions require profound faith, though the nature of what they have faith in differs considerably.

@UUID[Item.Ae6NFaTEysKIvBOO]{Priest's Zeal}

Requirement: One School of Magic

Willpower Points: —

Your mind fills you with inner fire. Whenever you cast a spell, your armor rating increases by one step for each WP you spend on casting the spell. The effect lasts until your turn in the next round.

@UUID[Item.B9kWg7ydZRZHLOOi]{Darkness}

Requirement: Priest's Zeal

Willpower Points: —

You know the general spell @UUID[Item.Shadowform0JkLmN]{Shadowform}. This spell is always prepared and does not count toward the number of spells you can hold prepared in your memory.

@UUID[Item.5neIjh4Z05m4hPQx]{Power Word: Shield}

Requirement: Priest's Zeal

Willpower Points: 2

If you or a creature within 10 meters of you is hit by an attack, spell, or monster attack, you can activate this ability to shield the target. The damage the target takes from the attack or spell is reduced by [[/roll 2D6]]. Using this ability can be done out of turn and does not count as an action.

@UUID[Item.XiExl4bRbWhp28v6]{Sanctify}

Requirement: Priest's Zeal

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability when casting a spell that heals a creature. You and all other creatures of your choice within 10 meters heal the same amount of HP.

Rogue

Azeroth's rogues are a diverse and pragmatic lot. Whether they operate as assassins in the service of SI:7, as independent operators selling their skills to the highest bidder, or as agents of their own inscrutable agendas, rogues share a commitment to efficiency, precision, and the advantages that come from going unseen. They are the world's poisoners, infiltrators, and opportunists, and occasionally its finest practitioners of the art of the perfectly placed blade.

In a world of armies and spellcasters and ancient powers, the rogue's greatest asset is the one nobody ever expects: information.

@UUID[Item.YGbcsXdT61RYTpjT]{Roguish Cunning}

Requirement: Knives 12

Willpower Points: —

Whenever you deal @UUID[JournalEntry.SbbSMsuvWeo3HaID.JournalEntryPage.KrSXg7HKmfo7xRcI#sneak-attack]{sneak attack} damage to a target, the dice increase for damage is increased by two dice instead of one (for example, 3D8 instead of 2D8 for a weapon that deals D8 damage).

@UUID[Item.Gey023AgZFHY2eWb]{Dirty Fighting}

Requirement: Roguish Cunning

Willpower Points: 3

This heroic ability can only be used if you wield a one-handed weapon in one hand and a one-handed ranged weapon in your other hand. The STR requirement of the weapon in your off hand (you decide whether it is right or left) increases by 3. You activate the ability on your turn in combat and can then perform an extra attack with your second weapon. The second attack is made with a bane. You decide in which order to use your two weapons. Finish the first attack, including damage, before rolling the second one.

@UUID[Item.lVzjJ1DfzMFTmOEs]{Envenom Weapons}

Requirement: Roguish Cunning

Willpower Points: 2

When you hit with a piercing or slashing weapon, you can activate this ability to also apply one dose of @UUID[JournalEntry.SbbSMsuvWeo3HaID.JournalEntryPage.6WPxPxUjh4W80RNy#poison]{poison} that you are carrying, as if it was ingested by the target. You can activate this ability after the roll to hit.

@UUID[Item.4ZvH6CerrczSUTeb]{Shadowstrike}

Requirement: Roguish Cunning

Willpower Points: 2

You teleport up to 20 meters to a spot that you can see and may immediately take an action. If the destination is covered in shade or darkness, the action is taken with a boon. You may then teleport back to your original spot.

Shaman

The shamans of Azeroth are intermediaries between the mortal world and the elemental spirits that pervade it. They do not command the elements so much as commune with them, entering into relationships of mutual respect with the spirits of fire, water, earth, and air. Elemental shamans channel this power into devastating offensive magic, calling down lightning and lava with the blessing of the spirits they serve. Enhancement shamans fight in close combat, their weapons empowered by elemental force.

Restoration shamans heal through cascading waves of spiritual energy that leap from ally to ally, their totem-anchored magic weaving a net of protection across the battlefield.

@UUID[Item.kSqCKYm8yIBWHo9Y]{Shamanic Calling}

Requirement: One School of Magic

Willpower Points: —

You know the general spell @UUID[Item.ElTotem1a2b3c4d5]{Elemental Totem}. This spell is always prepared and does not count toward the number of spells you can hold prepared in your memory.

You do not have to roll for LANGUAGES when communicating with or trying to understand elementals or their writing.

@UUID[Item.UfCB2AZHszINpPvJ]{Bloodlust}

Requirement: Shamanic Calling

Willpower Points: 3

Your howl makes your friends' blood boil. Activating this ability (an action in combat) gives all allies within 10 meters an extra action during their turn. The affected allies also become Angry, if they are not already. If an ally uses a reaction, or has already used one this round, they take their turn with no extra action, or may use another reaction. The effect lasts until your turn in the next round.

@UUID[Item.bIsyeDm1X7z6Hdi0]{Chain Heal}

Requirement: Shamanic Calling

Willpower Points: 2

When you heal with a spell or this ability, you can choose an additional creature within 10 meters of the target that was not healed by that spell or this ability. That creature receives the same amount of healing (roll separately). You can use this multiple times for the same spell casting, as long as you can pay the Willpower Points for each use.

@UUID[Item.MSPREyfVTRi4uUh3]{Stormstrike}

Requirement: Shamanic Calling

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability when you hit an enemy with a melee weapon, but before rolling for damage. The attack deals an extra D10 damage and is considered magical.

Warlock

The warlocks of Azeroth traffic in powers that most consider forbidden. Drawing on the energies of the Twisting Nether, the chaotic space between worlds where demons dwell, they bind demonic servants, curse their enemies with afflictions that fester and spread, and hurl bolts of pure fel energy with the casual confidence of those who have made their bargains and intend to collect. Warlocks are feared and distrusted across Azeroth, and for good reason.

The power they wield has a cost, though most warlocks will tell you the cost falls on someone else.

@UUID[Item.nLxCVDvXyvlLaXl1]{Warlock's Ambition}

Requirement: One School of Magic

Willpower Points: —

When you use @UUID[JournalEntry.BHzSGEPaCGVadFsb.JournalEntryPage.C0stUmhj95JFgL4f#power-level]{Power from the Body}, you get to keep any excess WP you do not use when casting the spell, up to your maximum WP.

@UUID[Item.MASYIf5D89N2pbIt]{Demonologist}

Requirement: Warlock's Ambition

Willpower Points: 3

You can use your action to activate this ability to instantly summon a demon into an empty space within 10 meters of you. Any demon you have already summoned using this heroic ability instantly disappears. The demon follows you for a shift at no additional WP cost. You can use its action in combat by paying the WP listed in its stat block (a free action for you). The demon can communicate with you in its demonic language, and you can both understand and speak it. The summoned demon is not necessarily the same individual you summoned previously. It is up to the GM whether the demon remembers encountering you before.

@UUID[Item.7jAxtKXRL0m8wBHo]{Life Drain}

Requirement: Warlock's Ambition

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability when you deal damage with a spell to one creature. You regain the same amount of HP as the creature lost.

@UUID[Item.hozY0JyCJR0crKbK]{Souls Collector}

Requirement: Warlock's Ambition

Willpower Points: 1

When you or an ally deals damage that brings another non-monster creature to 0 HP, you can activate this ability (no action) to store the enemy's soul in a soul shard. You can consume a shard as an action to recover [[/roll D3]] WP. Any remaining soul shards are lost when you finish a shift rest.

Warrior

The warriors of Azeroth are its backbone. They are not defined by magic or by divine favor, but by the simple fact that they are better at fighting than almost anyone else alive. Arms warriors wield massive two-handed weapons with tactical precision, reading the flow of battle and delivering devastating strikes at exactly the right moment. Fury warriors enter a frenzy of dual-wielded aggression, taking hits without slowing and hitting harder for it.

Protection warriors stand like walls between their allies and whatever threatens them, using every technique in their considerable arsenal to keep enemies focused on them and away from everyone else.

@UUID[Item.Zm1EbxNW5SL20lma]{Warrior's Rage}

Requirement: Axes, Hammers, or Swords 12

Willpower Points: —

You can wield a two-handed melee weapon in one hand. This can be combined with @UUID[Item.JrQqkQrSOFJzR7H9]{Dual Wield}.

@UUID[Item.JZPERHnYwztGbh5S]{Hamstring}

Requirement: Warrior's Rage

Willpower Points: 2

If an enemy tries to move away from you, you can activate this ability to make the enemy automatically fail its EVADE roll. If your free attack then hits, the enemy's movement is reduced to 0 until your turn in the next round. Using this ability can be done out of turn and does not count as an action.

@UUID[Item.69NxpqbxiReLf6zm]{Retaliation}

Requirement: Warrior's Rage

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability (no action) when an enemy within 2 meters of you deals damage to you with a melee attack. You immediately perform a counterattack on your opponent: an automatic hit with your weapon that cannot be dodged or parried.

@UUID[Item.LMt2nYu0xILSRUJy]{Sunder Armor}

Requirement: Warrior's Rage

Willpower Points: 3

You can activate this ability when you hit a creature with an attack to sunder its armor. For this attack and until your turn in the next round, the creature does not benefit from its armor rating.

Azeroth's adventurers use most of the same equipment described in the core rules, swords, bows, armor, and adventuring gear that would be recognizable in any fantasy setting. But the world of Warcraft has its own distinctive weapons and tools, a few of which have no direct equivalent in the standard equipment lists.

This chapter presents a small selection of new weapons inspired by Warcraft's most iconic martial traditions: the warglaives of the Illidari, the thrown glaives of night elf wardens, and others. These weapons follow all standard Dragonbane rules, with a few new properties defined here, and can be purchased, found, or crafted as described in the core rules.

All standard Dragonbane equipment remains available in Azeroth. A longsword is a longsword whether you're in Stormwind or Misty Vale, and the familiar equipment of Dragonbane requires no adaptation to work in this setting.

Firearms

Firearms are commonly available weapons, attributed to be originally crafted by the dwarves of Ironforge. In Bane of Azeroth it is represented by the secondary skill FIREARMS (AGL), which is available to anyone from start with a base chance like any other skill. Firing a firearm produces a loud boom, audible out to 500 meters.

Glaives

Warglaives and throwing glaives are typical elven weapons, used primarly by the illidari, wardens or troll shadow hunters. Attacks with glaives uses the KNIVES skill.

Melee Weapons

Freehanded: This weapon is strapped to your wrist and leaves a hand available to hold items, such as a torch or a focus. Attacks with this weapon uses the BRAWLING skill.

Scattershot: Attacks with this weapon do not get a bane for shooting at a target within 2 meters. For attacks beyond its listed range, damage is halved (round up).
